reasoning: 17 = -1 and 19 = 1 (mod 18). 29 is odd, so 17^29 = -1 and 19^29 = 1 (mod 18), and the sum is 0 (mod 18). Confirmed by direct modular exponentiation: (pow(17,29,18)+pow(19,29,18))%18 = 0.
solution: Modulo \(18\) we have \(17 \equiv -1\) and \(19 \equiv 1\). Since \(29\) is odd, \(17^{29} \equiv -1\) and \(19^{29} \equiv 1\), so the sum is \(\equiv -1 + 1 = 0\). The remainder is \(0\), that is, \(18\) divides \(17^{29} + 19^{29}\) exactly.

reasoning: Exponent of 2 in the product = 5 + 16 + 7 + 36 + 6 + 28 + 11 = 109; exponent of 5 = 3 + 6 + 12 + 14 + 30 = 65. n = min(109, 65) = 65. Both totals recomputed by summing prime valuations term by term.
solution: Each factor of \(10\) needs one \(2\) and one \(5\). Collecting powers of \(2\) from \(2^5, 4^8, 6^7, 8^{12}, 10^6, 20^{14}, 22^{11}\) gives \(5+16+7+36+6+28+11 = 109\), while powers of \(5\) from \(5^3, 10^6, 15^{12}, 20^{14}, 25^{15}\) give \(3+6+12+14+30 = 65\). The scarcer prime is \(5\), so the largest value is \(n = 65\).

reasoning: 4+7+9+8+6+5 = 39, so divisibility by 9 needs A+B congruent to 6 mod 9, i.e. A+B = 6 or 15. With B odd: (5,1), (3,3), (1,5), (8,7), (6,9). Exhaustive search over all 100 digit pairs returns exactly these five.
solution: The fixed digits \(4,7,9,8,6,5\) add to \(39\), so divisibility by \(9\) requires \(A+B \equiv 6 \pmod 9\), i.e. \(A+B = 6\) or \(A+B = 15\). Taking \(B\) odd, \(A+B=6\) allows \((A,B) = (5,1), (3,3), (1,5)\) and \(A+B=15\) allows \((8,7), (6,9)\). That is \(5\) pairs altogether.

reasoning: 999N = 1000N - N, so the last three digits are 1000 - N; setting 1000 - N = 132 gives N = 868 and the leading three digits are N - 1 = 867. Brute force over all three-digit N confirms 868 is the only one with 999N ending in 132.
solution: Since \(999 \times abc = 1000\,(abc) - abc\), the last three digits of the product are \(1000 - abc\). Setting \(1000 - abc = 132\) gives \(abc = 868\), and the leading three digits are \(868 - 1 = 867\). Indeed \(999 \times 868 = 867132\), so the six digits are \(8, 6, 8, 8, 6, 7\).

reasoning: At 6 p.m. the first car is 60 km ahead; the second gains 20 km/hr and catches it 3 hours later at 9 p.m., 240 km from the start. The third travels 240 km in the 2 hours from 7 p.m. to 9 p.m., so x = 120.
solution: By 6 p.m. the first car is \(60\) km ahead, and the second closes the gap at \(20\) km/hr, so it draws level \(3\) hours later at 9 p.m., \(240\) km from the starting point. The third car leaves at 7 p.m. and must cover that same \(240\) km by 9 p.m., i.e. in \(2\) hours. Hence \(x = 120\) km/hr.

reasoning: a-4 = m^3 and a+4 = n^2 with m not 1 gives n^2 - m^3 = 8, so m = 2, n = 4 and a = 12. The target age A needs A-1 a perfect square and A+1 a perfect cube; an exhaustive scan to 10^6 returns A = 26 uniquely (25 = 5^2, 27 = 3^3). Wait = 26 - 12 = 14.
solution: If her present age is \(a\), then \(a-4\) is a cube and \(a+4\) a square, so \(n^2 - m^3 = 8\); with \(m \neq 1\) this forces \(m = 2\), \(n = 4\) and \(a = 12\). She next wants an age \(A\) with \(A-1\) a perfect square and \(A+1\) a perfect cube, and \(A = 26\) is the only such age, since \(25 = 5^2\) and \(27 = 3^3\). So she must wait \(26 - 12 = 14\) years.

value: the claim that every number of the form 6n - 1 is prime
reasoning: 6n-1 is composite at n = 6 (35 = 5 x 7) and n = 11 (65), so that statement is false. The other three are true: two odd primes differ by an even number; Euclid's lemma; and a scan to 2000 finds (3,5,7) as the only prime triplet p, p+2, p+4.
solution: Numbers of the form \(6n-1\) need not be prime: at \(n=6\) it is \(35 = 5 \times 7\). The other three claims hold — two primes above \(2\) are both odd so their difference is even, Euclid's lemma gives the divisibility property of a prime, and \((3,5,7)\) is the only triple of primes with successive gaps of \(2\). The untrue statement is therefore the one asserting that every \(6n-1\) is prime.

reasoning: x + (x+2)/(2x) = x + 1/2 + 1/x. For x > 0, x + 1/x has minimum 2 at x = 1, so the minimum is 5/2. sympy minimum() on (0, inf) returns 5/2.
solution: Rewrite the expression as \(x + \dfrac{x+2}{2x} = x + \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{x}\). For \(x > 0\) the sum \(x + \dfrac{1}{x}\) is least when \(x = 1\), where it equals \(2\). The minimum value is therefore \(2 + \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{5}{2}\).

value: x = plus or minus (1/p) sqrt((2p - q)/q), with 2p not equal to q
reasoning: Squaring gives (1+px)^2(1-qx) = (1-px)^2(1+qx), which reduces to 2x(2p - q - p^2 q x^2) = 0. The non-zero roots are x^2 = (2p-q)/(p^2 q). Checked numerically at p = 3, q = 4: x = +/-0.235702 makes the printed left side equal 1.000000 for both signs, while the p-q forms (options with sqrt(p-q)) are imaginary there and the q/p sqrt(2p-q) form gives 1.886, not a root.
solution: Squaring both sides gives \((1+px)^2(1-qx) = (1-px)^2(1+qx)\). Expanding and cancelling reduces this to \(2x\left(2p - q - p^2qx^2\right) = 0\), and discarding \(x=0\) leaves \(x^2 = \dfrac{2p-q}{p^2q}\). Hence \(x = \pm\dfrac{1}{p}\sqrt{\dfrac{2p-q}{q}}\), which requires \(2p \neq q\) so that the root is non-zero.

reasoning: Collection = rent x rooms, so it is multiplied by 1.2 x 1.2 = 1.44, an increase of 44%.
solution: The total collection is the rent per room multiplied by the number of rooms, so it is scaled by \(1.2 \times 1.2 = 1.44\). That is an increase of \(44\%\).

reasoning: d/8 - d/10 = 9/60 gives d/40 = 3/20, so d = 6. sympy solve confirms d = 6.
solution: If the school is \(d\) km away, the time difference is \(\dfrac{d}{8} - \dfrac{d}{10} = \dfrac{9}{60}\) hour. This simplifies to \(\dfrac{d}{40} = \dfrac{3}{20}\), so \(d = 6\) km.

reasoning: With t = 3^x, 9t + 1/t = 10 gives 9t^2 - 10t + 1 = 0, so t = 1 or 1/9, i.e. x = 0 or x = -2. sympy solve returns [-2, 0].
solution: Put \(t = 3^x\), so the equation becomes \(9t + \dfrac{1}{t} = 10\), i.e. \(9t^2 - 10t + 1 = 0\). Its roots are \(t = 1\) and \(t = \dfrac{1}{9}\), which correspond to \(x = 0\) and \(x = -2\).

value: none of 17, 29 or 43 — the primes are 2, 31 and 67
reasoning: Three odd primes sum to an odd number, so one prime must be 2 and the other two sum to 98; a difference of 36 gives 67 and 31, both prime. An exhaustive search over all prime triples summing to 100 with some pair differing by 36 returns [2, 31, 67] as the unique triple, and none of 17, 29, 43 belongs to it.
solution: Three odd primes would give an odd total, so one of the primes must be \(2\) and the other two add to \(98\). A difference of \(36\) then gives \(67\) and \(31\), both prime, and this is the only triple satisfying the conditions. Since none of \(17\), \(29\) or \(43\) is among \(2, 31, 67\), none of the listed values can be one of the numbers.

reasoning: Working outwards: 23/16 = 1 + 7/16 gives a = 1; 16/7 = 2 + 2/7 gives b = 2; c + 1/2 = 7/2 gives c = 3. Mean = 2. Exact Fraction search over a, b, c in 1..9 finds only (1, 2, 3).
solution: Inverting, \(a + \dfrac{1}{\cdots} = \dfrac{23}{16} = 1 + \dfrac{7}{16}\), so \(a = 1\). Next \(b + \dfrac{1}{\cdots} = \dfrac{16}{7} = 2 + \dfrac{2}{7}\), so \(b = 2\), and finally \(c + \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{7}{2}\) gives \(c = 3\). The mean of \(1, 2, 3\) is \(2\).

reasoning: Reading the pairwise figures as full intersections (the only consistent reading — treating them as 'exactly two' would make 'only I' equal 10-8-2-1 = -1), only I = 10-8-2+1 = 1%, only II = 30-8-4+1 = 19%, only III = 5-4-2+1 = 0%. Total 20% of 1,00,000 = 20,000.
solution: Readers of the first paper alone number \(10 - 8 - 2 + 1 = 1\%\), of the second alone \(30 - 8 - 4 + 1 = 19\%\) and of the third alone \(5 - 4 - 2 + 1 = 0\%\). Together that is \(20\%\) of the town, i.e. \(20{,}000\) people.

reasoning: At least two = sum of pairwise overlaps minus twice the triple overlap = 8 + 4 + 2 - 2(1) = 12%. Cross-checked as exactly two (7 + 3 + 1 = 11%) plus all three (1%) = 12%. 12% of 1,00,000 = 12,000.
solution: Adding the three pairwise figures counts the all-three group three times, so readers of at least two papers are \(8 + 4 + 2 - 2(1) = 12\%\). Equivalently, exactly two accounts for \(7 + 3 + 1 = 11\%\) and all three for \(1\%\). That is \(12\%\) of \(1{,}00{,}000\), i.e. \(12{,}000\) people.

reasoning: Union = 10 + 30 + 5 - 8 - 4 - 2 + 1 = 32%, so none = 68%, i.e. 68,000. Consistent with 20% (only one) + 11% (exactly two) + 1% (all three) = 32%.
solution: By inclusion and exclusion the readers of at least one paper form \(10 + 30 + 5 - 8 - 4 - 2 + 1 = 32\%\) of the town. Hence \(100 - 32 = 68\%\) read none of them, which is \(68{,}000\) people.

reasoning: Unit digits of powers of 7 cycle 7, 9, 3, 1 with period 4; 73 = 4(18) + 1, so the unit digit is 7. pow(7,73,10) = 7.
solution: The unit digits of \(7, 7^2, 7^3, 7^4\) are \(7, 9, 3, 1\), after which the pattern repeats with period \(4\). Since \(73 = 4 \times 18 + 1\), the unit digit of \(7^{73}\) is the first in that cycle, namely \(7\).

reasoning: n^2 + 48 = m^2 gives (m-n)(m+n) = 48 with both factors even: (2,24), (4,12), (6,8), yielding n = 11, 4, 1. A direct scan of n up to 10000 returns exactly [1, 4, 11].
solution: If \(n^2 + 48 = m^2\) then \((m-n)(m+n) = 48\), and the two factors must have the same parity, so both are even. The even factor pairs \((2,24), (4,12), (6,8)\) give \(n = 11, 4, 1\) respectively. So there are exactly three such positive integers.

reasoning: Put a = 2sqrt2, b = 2sqrt3; then 4sqrt6 = ab and sqrt2 + sqrt3 = (a+b)/2, so x = 2ab/(a+b). Then (x+a)/(x-a) = (a+3b)/(b-a) and (x+b)/(x-b) = -(b+3a)/(b-a), whose sum is (2b-2a)/(b-a) = 2. sympy simplify of the original expression returns exactly 2.
solution: Write \(a = 2\sqrt{2}\) and \(b = 2\sqrt{3}\). Since \(ab = 4\sqrt{6}\) and \(\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{a+b}{2}\), the given value is \(x = \dfrac{2ab}{a+b}\). Then \(\dfrac{x+a}{x-a} = \dfrac{a+3b}{b-a}\) and \(\dfrac{x+b}{x-b} = -\dfrac{b+3a}{b-a}\), and their sum collapses to \(\dfrac{2b-2a}{b-a} = 2\).
Take \(x = 0.3z\) and \(y = 0.4z\), so \(\dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{0.3}{0.4} = \dfrac{3}{4}\). Since \(x\) is \(p\%\) of \(y\), we need \(\dfrac{p}{100} = \dfrac{3}{4}\), giving \(p = 75\).

reasoning: The plane passes vertically over P, so P lies on the ground circle it traces. Angular speed is 360/180 = 2 deg/s, so t and t+30 are 60 degrees apart. Equal elevation means equal horizontal distance from P, so the two positions are reflections in the line joining the centre to P: theta and -theta. Hence theta_t + 60 = -theta_t (mod 360), giving theta_t = -30 or 150. A scan of theta_0 in 0.1-degree steps returns exactly these, with x = 15 and x = 105 respectively. Only 105 is a printed option; the other configuration (the plane crossing over P between the two instants) would give 15 seconds.
solution: Because the plane later passes vertically over the point, that point lies on the circle its shadow traces; one round in \(180\) seconds means it turns \(2^\circ\) per second, so the two instants are \(60^\circ\) apart. Equal angles of elevation mean equal horizontal distances, so the two positions are mirror images in the line joining the centre of the circle to the point — which places the plane \(210^\circ\) short of that point at time \(t\). Covering \(210^\circ\) takes \(\dfrac{210}{2} = 105\) seconds, so \(x = 105\).

reasoning: Coprime pairs above 1 illustrating each case: (2,3) both prime; (4,9) both composite; (2,9) one prime one composite. All three statements are possible.
solution: Two coprime integers greater than \(1\) can both be prime, as with \(2\) and \(3\); both composite, as with \(4\) and \(9\), which share no prime factor; or one of each, as with \(2\) and \(9\). All three statements are therefore correct.
With \(g\) girls and \(100-g\) boys, the total weight gives \(24g + 32(100-g) = 30 \times 100\). This reduces to \(3200 - 8g = 3000\), so \(g = 25\).

value: positive only if a is not equal to b
reasoning: The expression equals |a-b| + |b-a| = 2|a-b|, which is 0 when a = b and positive otherwise. Checked at (3,3) -> 0, (3,5) -> 4, (5,3) -> 4, so it is not always zero, not never zero, and not tied to a > b.
solution: Since \(\sqrt{u^2} = |u|\), the expression equals \(|a-b| + |b-a| = 2|a-b|\). This vanishes exactly when \(a=b\) and is positive otherwise, so it is positive precisely when \(a \neq b\) — the direction of the inequality between \(a\) and \(b\) is irrelevant.

reasoning: With a = k, b = 6k, c = m, d = 6m, the ratio is (k^2+m^2)/(36(k^2+m^2)) = 1/36.
solution: Write \(a = k, b = 6k, c = m, d = 6m\). Then \(\dfrac{a^2+c^2}{b^2+d^2} = \dfrac{k^2+m^2}{36k^2+36m^2} = \dfrac{1}{36}\), independent of \(k\) and \(m\).

reasoning: 0.53 recurring (both digits) = 53/99; 0.5 with 3 recurring = 48/90 = 8/15. Sum = 265/495 + 264/495 = 529/495. Decimal expansion to 30 places is 1.06868686868686868686868686869, i.e. a single 0 then the block 68 repeating. The rivals evaluate to 1.068888... , 1.068068068... and 1.068 exactly, all different.
solution: Here \(0.\overline{53} = \dfrac{53}{99}\) and \(0.5\overline{3} = \dfrac{53-5}{90} = \dfrac{8}{15}\). Their sum is \(\dfrac{265}{495} + \dfrac{264}{495} = \dfrac{529}{495}\), and long division gives \(1.0686868\ldots\). The recurring block is \(68\) and it begins only after a single \(0\), so the value is \(1.0\overline{68}\).

reasoning: 3^1 = 3 > 1, 3^2 = 9 > 8, 3^3 = 27 = 27 (fails), and 3^N > N^3 for all N >= 4 (checked to N = 7 and true thereafter since 3^N grows faster). So the inequality holds for every natural number other than 3.
solution: Testing small values, \(3^1 > 1^3\) and \(3^2 = 9 > 8 = 2^3\) both hold, while \(3^3 = 27\) merely equals \(3^3\) and so fails a strict inequality. From \(N = 4\) onwards \(3^N\) outstrips \(N^3\) and never falls back. The inequality therefore holds for every natural number apart from \(3\).

reasoning: 59049 = 3^10, so its square root is 243, rational. 231/593 is a ratio of integers. 0.454545... is a repeating decimal, hence rational. The last decimal has ever-lengthening blocks of 1s and 2s, so it never becomes periodic and is irrational.
solution: Here \(\sqrt{59049} = 243\) because \(59049 = 3^{10}\), \(\dfrac{231}{593}\) is a ratio of integers, and \(0.454545\ldots\) is a repeating decimal — all three are rational. The decimal \(0.12112211122211112222\ldots\) has blocks of \(1\)s and \(2\)s that keep growing, so it never settles into a repeating pattern and is irrational.

reasoning: Distances: 9(50/60) = 7.5, 8(80/60) = 32/3, 7.5(100/60) = 12.5 km, total 92/3 km. Total time 230/60 = 23/6 hours. Average speed = (92/3)/(23/6) = 8 exactly. The plain mean of the three speeds is 8.1667, which is the trap.
solution: The three legs cover \(9 \times \dfrac{50}{60} = 7.5\) km, \(8 \times \dfrac{80}{60} = \dfrac{32}{3}\) km and \(7.5 \times \dfrac{100}{60} = 12.5\) km, a total of \(\dfrac{92}{3}\) km in \(\dfrac{230}{60} = \dfrac{23}{6}\) hours. Average speed is total distance divided by total time, \(\dfrac{92/3}{23/6} = 8\) kmph. Averaging the three speeds directly would wrongly give \(8.17\) kmph, since the legs take unequal times.

reasoning: If a+b+c is non-zero, adding numerators and denominators gives (a+b+c)/(2(a+b+c)) = 1/2. If a+b+c = 0 then b+c = -a and each ratio is -1; verified at (a,b,c) = (1,1,-2) where all three fractions equal -1, and at (1,1,1) where all equal 1/2.
solution: If \(a+b+c \neq 0\), adding the numerators and denominators of the equal ratios gives \(\dfrac{a+b+c}{2(a+b+c)} = \dfrac{1}{2}\). If instead \(a+b+c = 0\), then \(b+c = -a\) and each fraction is \(\dfrac{a}{-a} = -1\). So every fraction equals \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) or \(-1\).
Since \(3^2 = 9 \equiv 1 \pmod 8\), we have \(3^{520} = (3^2)^{260} \equiv 1\). Multiplying by one more factor of \(3\) gives \(3^{521} \equiv 3 \pmod 8\), so the remainder is \(3\).

runnerUpIf: the question is read as covering only primes with more than one digit, which removes 2 and 5 and leaves the four digits 1, 3, 7, 9
reasoning: Taking all primes, the set of unit digits is {1,2,3,5,7,9}: 11, 2, 3, 5, 7, 19 supply them. A scan of primes below 10000 returns exactly that set, with no prime ending in 0, 4, 6 or 8. So 6 digits. RUNNER-UP: 4, if the question is silently restricted to multi-digit primes, since 2 and 5 are then excluded; nothing in the printed stem imposes that restriction.
solution: A prime can end in \(1\) (as in \(11\)), \(2\) (as in \(2\)), \(3\), \(5\), \(7\) or \(9\) (as in \(19\)). No prime ends in \(0, 4, 6\) or \(8\), since such a number is even and larger than \(2\). That leaves \(6\) possible unit digits — though if one had in mind only primes of more than one digit, \(2\) and \(5\) would drop out and just \(4\) would remain.

reasoning: The swing from a 6% loss to a 6% gain is 12% of the cost price, so 0.12C = 6 and C = 50.
solution: Selling at a \(6\%\) gain rather than a \(6\%\) loss changes the amount received by \(12\%\) of the cost price. So if the cost price is \(C\), then \(0.12\,C = 6\), giving \(C = 50\) rupees.

reasoning: One man does 1/168 of the field per day and one woman 1/252. Then 8(1/168) + 16(1/252) = 1/21 + 4/63 = 1/9, so the job takes 9 days. Exact Fraction arithmetic gives 9.
solution: Since \(12\) men need \(14\) days, one man does \(\dfrac{1}{168}\) of the field per day; likewise one woman does \(\dfrac{1}{252}\). Together, \(8\) men and \(16\) women complete \(\dfrac{8}{168} + \dfrac{16}{252} = \dfrac{1}{21} + \dfrac{4}{63} = \dfrac{1}{9}\) of the field each day. The whole field therefore takes \(9\) days.

reasoning: With 3^x = 4^y = 12^z = k, we have 1/x = log3/log k, 1/y = log4/log k, 1/z = log12/log k, and log 12 = log 3 + log 4, so 1/z = 1/x + 1/y. Numerically with k = 15: z = 1.0897996 and xy/(x+y) = 1.0897996, matching to 15 digits, while xy = 4.815, x+y = 4.418 and 4x+3y = 15.72 do not.
solution: Let \(3^x = 4^y = 12^z = k\), so that \(x = \dfrac{\log k}{\log 3}\), \(y = \dfrac{\log k}{\log 4}\) and \(z = \dfrac{\log k}{\log 12}\). Because \(\log 12 = \log 3 + \log 4\), this gives \(\dfrac{1}{z} = \dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{y}\). Rearranging, \(z = \dfrac{xy}{x+y}\).

reasoning: Expanding both sides and subtracting gives -56(ad - bc) = 0 (confirmed by sympy factor), so ad = bc, which on dividing by bd gives a/b = c/d.
solution: Expanding both products, every term cancels except the cross terms, leaving \(-56(ad - bc) = 0\). Hence \(ad = bc\), and dividing through by \(bd\) gives \(\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{c}{d}\).

value: a = 0 and b may be any integer
runnerUpIf: the paper wanted one particular admissible pair rather than the general characterisation, since a = 0 with b = 3 does satisfy the condition
reasoning: By the remainder theorem the two remainders are f(1) = 1+a+b and f(-1) = 1-a+b. Equating gives 2a = 0, so a = 0 while b is entirely unconstrained. RUNNER-UP: the pair 0 and 3, which is a true particular instance (x^2+3 leaves remainder 4 on division by both x-1 and x+1) and would win if the examiner intended a single numeric pair. The pairs with a = 4 or a = 3 are simply wrong.
solution: By the remainder theorem the two remainders are \(f(1) = 1 + a + b\) and \(f(-1) = 1 - a + b\). Setting them equal gives \(2a = 0\), so \(a = 0\), while nothing at all constrains \(b\). Hence \(a\) is \(0\) and \(b\) may be any integer; particular choices such as \(b = 3\) do work, but only as instances of this general result.

reasoning: Combined rate = 1/6 + 1/10 = 4/15 per hour, so the time is 15/4 = 3.75 hours = 3 h 45 min.
solution: In one hour they finish \(\dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{4}{15}\) of the work. The whole task therefore needs \(\dfrac{15}{4} = 3.75\) hours, that is, \(3\) hours and \(45\) minutes.

runnerUpIf: the leading 2 were meant to sit under the first radical, giving the familiar nested radical whose value is 2
reasoning: Solved as printed, with the leading '2 +' OUTSIDE the radical. Let y be the nested radical; then y^2 = 2 + y, so y = 2 (the root -1 is rejected). The printed expression is 2 + y = 4. Iterating y -> sqrt(2+y) from 0 converges to 2.000000, giving 4.000000. RUNNER-UP: 2, the value if the leading 2 belongs inside the first radical — the standard form of this problem. Both 2 and 4 appear among the printed options, so a typesetting slip here would flip the answer; flagged, not corrected.
solution: Let \(y = \sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2 + \sqrt{\ldots}}}\), the repeating part of the expression. Then \(y^2 = 2 + y\), whose admissible root is \(y = 2\), the value \(-1\) being impossible for a square root. The expression as printed adds a further \(2\) outside the radical, so its value is \(2 + 2 = 4\); note that if the leading \(2\) were meant to lie under the first radical the value would instead be \(2\), and both readings appear among the choices.

reasoning: Failing at least one = 52 + 42 - 17 = 77%, so passing both = 100 - 77 = 23%.
solution: Candidates failing at least one subject number \(52 + 42 - 17 = 77\%\), the subtraction removing the double count of those failing both. Everyone else passed in both subjects, so that is \(100 - 77 = 23\%\).

reasoning: With the wife's share w, each daughter gets 2w and each son 6w, so w + 5(6w) + 4(2w) = 39w = 3,90,000 and w = 10,000.
solution: Let the wife's share be \(w\); each daughter then receives \(2w\) and each son \(3 \times 2w = 6w\). The total is \(w + 5(6w) + 4(2w) = 39w\), and setting \(39w = 3{,}90{,}000\) gives \(w = 10{,}000\) rupees.

reasoning: Need (1.4)^n > 3. Computed: 1.4, 1.96, 2.744, 3.8416 — the first year exceeding 3 is the fourth.
solution: After \(n\) years the sum is multiplied by \((1.4)^n\), and we need this to exceed \(3\). Now \((1.4)^3 = 2.744\), which is still short, while \((1.4)^4 = 3.8416\) is more than treble. So \(4\) complete years are needed.

reasoning: Equal interest over the same period gives 5a = 6b = 9c, so a : b : c = 1/5 : 1/6 : 1/9 = 18 : 15 : 10. With 43 parts making 17,200, one part is 400 and the 9% part is 4,000. sympy solve returns a = 7200, b = 6000, c = 4000.
solution: Since the three interests are equal over the same two years, \(5a = 6b = 9c\), so \(a : b : c = \dfrac{1}{5} : \dfrac{1}{6} : \dfrac{1}{9} = 18 : 15 : 10\). These \(43\) parts make up \(17{,}200\), so one part is \(400\). The amount invested at \(9\%\) is \(10 \times 400 = 4{,}000\) rupees.

reasoning: The three brackets sum to zero, and u+v+w = 0 implies u^3+v^3+w^3 = 3uvw, so the numerator equals the denominator. sympy simplify returns 1.
solution: The three quantities \((x-y), (y-z), (z-x)\) add to \(0\), and whenever \(u + v + w = 0\) one has \(u^3 + v^3 + w^3 = 3uvw\). So the numerator is exactly \(3(x-y)(y-z)(z-x)\), and the quotient is \(1\).

reasoning: With a^x = b^y = c^z = k, a = k^(1/x), b = k^(1/y), c = k^(1/z). Then b^2 = ac reads k^(2/y) = k^(1/x + 1/z), so 1/x + 1/z = 2/y. Numerically with 1/x = 1/3, 1/z = 1/7 and y chosen accordingly, b^2 = 2.15200293 and ac = 2.15200293 agree to 15 digits.
solution: Let \(a^x = b^y = c^z = k\), so that \(a = k^{1/x}\), \(b = k^{1/y}\) and \(c = k^{1/z}\). The condition \(b^2 = ac\) becomes \(k^{2/y} = k^{1/x + 1/z}\). Comparing exponents gives \(\dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{z} = \dfrac{2}{y}\).

reasoning: p + q = 15 and p - q = 1 give p = 8, q = 7, so r = pq = 56.
solution: The sum of the roots is \(p + q = 15\) and we are told \(p - q = 1\), so \(p = 8\) and \(q = 7\). The product of the roots is \(r\), hence \(r = 8 \times 7 = 56\).

reasoning: x^2 - 7x + 12 = (x-3)(x-4) > 0 exactly when both factors share a sign, i.e. x < 3 or x > 4. sympy solveset returns Union(Interval.open(-oo,3), Interval.open(4,oo)).
solution: Factorising, \(x^2 - 7x + 12 = (x-3)(x-4)\), and a product of two factors is positive only when both have the same sign. That happens for \(x < 3\) and again for \(x > 4\). The solution set is therefore \(-\infty < x < 3\) or \(4 < x < \infty\); either interval alone is incomplete.

reasoning: 5^(2n) - 2^(3n) = 25^n - 8^n, and a^n - b^n is always divisible by a - b = 17. Factorisations: n=1 gives 17; n=2 gives 3 x 11 x 17; n=3 gives 7 x 17 x 127. So 17 divides it for every n while 3 and 7 fail at n = 1.
solution: Rewrite the expression as \(5^{2n} - 2^{3n} = 25^n - 8^n\). Since \(a^n - b^n\) is always divisible by \(a-b\), this is divisible by \(25 - 8 = 17\) for every \(n\). Checking small cases, \(n=1\) gives \(17\) itself and \(n=2\) gives \(561 = 3 \times 11 \times 17\), so neither \(3\) nor \(7\) is a factor in general.
